findings.source_passage: this savage's sword, thought I, which thus finally shapes and fashions both warp and woof; this easy, indifferent sword must be chance—aye, chance, free will, and necessity—nowise incompatible
findings.source_locator: second paragraph, after 'final aspect of the completed fabric'
findings.why_it_matters: The explicit philosophic identification—'this savage's sword, thought I, which thus finally shapes and fashions both warp and woof'—is the interpretive keystone of the entire chapter; it names chance as the agent and attributes it specifically to the savage's sword. The draft collapses this into 'shaped the fabric; this easy, indifferent sword must be chance,' losing the syntactic repetition and the explicit 'shapes and fashions both warp and woof' framing that makes the allegory legible.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'this savage's sword, thought I, which thus finally shapes and fashions both warp and woof; this easy, indifferent sword must be chance—aye, chance, free will, and necessity—nowise incompatible—all interweavingly working together.' The full formulation is the philosophic payoff and must appear verbatim or near-verbatim.

findings.source_passage: by this difference in the concluding blow producing a corresponding contrast in the final aspect of the completed fabric
findings.source_locator: second paragraph, after 'or strongly, or weakly, as the case might be'
findings.why_it_matters: This causal link—that the variation in Queequeg's sword-blow produces a 'corresponding contrast in the final aspect of the completed fabric'—is the logical bridge that makes the chance-allegory coherent. Without it the philosophical argument loses its mechanical grounding and reads as mere assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the clause: 'and by this difference in the concluding blow producing a corresponding contrast in the final aspect of the completed fabric' before the identification of the sword with chance.

findings.source_passage: I started at a sound so strange, long drawn, and musically wild and unearthly, that the ball of free will dropped from my hand
findings.why_it_matters: The source reads 'when I started at a sound'—the verb 'started' carries the physical shock that literalizes the dropping of the 'ball of free will.' The draft's 'when a sound… came' is grammatically passive and loses that jolt, weakening the ironic echo of the philosophical framework just established.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I started at a sound' to preserve the physical-philosophical pun.

findings.source_passage: from few of those lungs could that accustomed old cry have derived such a marvellous cadence as from Tashtego the Indian's
findings.source_locator: third paragraph, after 'hundreds of whalemen's look-outs perched as high in the air'
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence establishes Tashtego's singular voice and the 'marvellous cadence' motif, which prepares the prophet/seer simile in the next paragraph. Its omission makes the transition to the seer image feel unanchored and reduces Tashtego to a generic lookout.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the comparative sentence about Tashtego's marvellous cadence before the prophet simile paragraph.

summary: The draft drops the philosophically critical 'shapes and fashions both warp and woof' identification—the allegorical climax of the chapter—and suppresses two additional medium-weight passages, collectively degrading the interpretive coherence of the Loom of Time sequence.
